open-question.question: The goal names the runtime files, the CLAUDE.md invariants, and the rebuilt hosts/ trees as this milestone's deliverables and says nothing about docs/. Should any page under docs/ (for example the "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md or the entries of docs/skill-reference.md) describe the literal-path rule and the full-command rule, or do the docs stay unchanged?
open-question.recommendation: Both rules govern how a runner writes a shell command and change no step, commit, subject, or file a docs reader would see, so docs/ has no behaviour to describe; the runtime files and the `CLAUDE.md` invariant bullet are their homes, the goal lists no docs deliverable, and one more copy in prose that no gate checks could only drift.
open-question.alternative: No page under docs/ is edited in this milestone. Neither rule is described anywhere in docs/. The literal-path rule and the full-command rule are stated only in the runtime files and in the CLAUDE.md invariant bullet. This means never as part of this milestone, and any later docs pass is free to add them. This matches the goal exactly, which lists the runtime files, the CLAUDE.md invariants, and the rebuilt hosts/ trees as the deliverables and does not mention docs/. The change alters nothing a user sees: no skill gains or loses a step, a commit, a subject, or a file. The docs describe workflow behaviour at that user-visible level, so the rules have no behaviour to describe there. docs/ is not a build input to hosts/, and neither --check nor pytest reads it, so nothing in the done-when gate depends on it. The rules also get no third copy that could drift. The "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md already spells out the staging mechanics ("path-scoped (only the paths it touched, never `git add -A`)", with core/shared/commit-procedure.md as their home). A contributor who learns the commit mechanics from that section is not told that the paths must also appear literally. This also departs from the recent habit of updating docs in the same milestone as an invariant change, as in "Update Invariant And Docs For Committing Bootstrap", although those milestones changed user-visible behaviour and this one does not.

Only the "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md changes. The sentence that names core/shared/commit-procedure.md and its path-scoped staging gains one clause: each path is named literally on the command line, never through a shell variable. The rationale stays in CLAUDE.md. The full-command rule for open-question tool calls is not described in docs/, and docs/skill-reference.md and docs/design-claims.md are unchanged. The rule goes in the one docs passage that already describes the same mechanics at the same level of detail. That passage names the never-`git add -A` ban and the commit procedure, so a one-clause addition keeps it accurate without opening a new topic. The edit is minimal and local. The two rules this milestone adds as a pair are documented unevenly. The full-command rule covers five sites and the command they share, but it gets no docs mention, so a reader of docs/ sees half of the fix. This also adds one more copy of the commit-procedure wording, which a later change to the rule must keep in step.

Only docs/design-claims.md changes. One ASD-STE100 design sentence is added under an existing claim, most naturally claim 18 ("The same behaviour on each host"), or else claim 12 ("Repository hygiene is structural"). It states both rules together: commit paths are written literally and tool commands are written in full on every call, never through a shell variable, alias, or function, so a run behaves the same whatever shell runs it. docs/workflow.md and docs/skill-reference.md are unchanged. Both rules are cross-cutting robustness guarantees, not features of any single skill, and the claims page is where cross-cutting guarantees and their designs are listed. One sentence covers both provoking sites at the level of a guarantee, with no copy of the per-site mechanics to drift. Claim 18 and its metric ("Same case scores on each host tree") are about host definitions, not the shell a host runs commands in, and claim 12's metric does not test word splitting either. The new sentence would therefore sit under a metric that does not check it, unless the metric is reworded too. Meanwhile the "How skills commit" passage, which describes the staging mechanics directly, stays silent.

Two pages change. The "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md gains the literal-path clause next to its existing path-scoped staging and commit-procedure wording. docs/design-claims.md gains one STE design sentence, under claim 18 or claim 12, stating both rules together as a shell-neutral guarantee. docs/skill-reference.md is unchanged, so the full-command rule appears in docs/ only at the level of a claim. Both rules are documented, and each sits at the altitude of the page that holds it. The commit rule goes where the staging mechanics already live, and the pair is stated once as a guarantee on the claims page. No per-skill entry is restated. The edit touches two pages that use different registers: the workflow prose, and the STE-controlled claims page with its claim-and-metric structure. The same claim-metric mismatch as for a claim line alone applies. The commit rule then appears in four places (commit-procedure.md, complete-task.md, CLAUDE.md, and workflow.md), which a later change to the rule must keep matching.

Two pages change. The "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md gains the literal-path clause. In docs/skill-reference.md, the entries of the multi-call open-question tool sites gain the full-command rule: review-milestone-requirements, provide-alternatives-to-all-open-questions, recommend-all-open-questions, and answer-all-open-questions-with-recommendation, plus the answer-skill entries that follow answer-procedure.md. Each entry says that every call writes the full command, never through a variable, alias, or function of the runner's own. docs/design-claims.md is unchanged. Every docs passage that describes an affected mechanic is brought into line with the runtime. Several skill-reference entries already describe their tool calls in detail (for example the alternatives pass "in two calls to the open-question tool"), and they would now say how those calls are written. A reader of any one entry sees the rule that governs it. One runtime sentence is restated across five or more skill-reference entries, which are already long. That is the kind of per-site copy claim 17 counts against, and each copy can drift from the clause stated once in each runtime file. Whether the provide-alternatives-to-open-question (subagent) entry also needs the rule depends on how the sibling question about the alternatives agent's coverage settles.

Every docs page that touches the affected mechanics changes. The "How skills commit" section of docs/workflow.md gains the literal-path clause. The docs/skill-reference.md entries of the multi-call tool sites, including the answer skills that follow answer-procedure.md, gain the full-command rule. docs/design-claims.md gains one STE design sentence, under claim 18 or claim 12, stating both rules as a shell-neutral guarantee. This gives the most complete documentation. A contributor finds the rules wherever they look in docs/, whether that is the commit narrative, the per-skill reference, or the guarantees page, in the same way the bootstrap-committing milestone updated all three pages together with its invariant. It is the largest change for a fix that alters no user-visible behaviour. It goes well past the goal's deliverables and puts the most copies of the two rules into hand-maintained prose that no gate checks. It also carries the claim-metric mismatch on the claims page. Whether the subagent's skill-reference entry is included depends on how the sibling question about the alternatives agent's coverage settles.
